page_title: 🏈 Rugby: Optimise CocoaPods project | Swifty Finch

summary.name: Rugby
summary.one_liner: Rugby is a Swift command-line utility that speeds up Xcode work on large CocoaPods projects by building secondary pod targets and removing them from the Pods project.
use_cases: speed up Xcode on a large project with many CocoaPods
avoid endless indexing of remote pod targets
keep Podfile and Podfile.lock unchanged while optimising pods
replace slow Ruby scripts for CocoaPods build tweaks
summary.what_it_does: The page is a write-up of the author's journey to fix slow Xcode performance on a huge CocoaPods project. The author describes trying a separate Xcode project, disabling Xcode indexing via a defaults command, buying a MacBook Air M1, and finally writing Rugby. Rugby builds the secondary pod targets and removes them from the Pods project, so only a small share of targets (around ten percent, per the author) stays in the project. The tool is written in Swift, not Ruby, and does not modify Podfile or Podfile.lock, which the author says matters on a team. The page says a beta test with about 30 users was run and a stable release with a new beta command shipped. More details are on GitHub, which the page links to but does not describe in detail.
notable: Does not change Podfile or Podfile.lock, so teammates with their own tasks are not affected
Written in Swift as a command-line utility, using SPM packages
Removes secondary pod targets from the Pods project to cut indexing and rebuild time
caveats: The page does not state a license; pricing is inferred as open source only from the author's invitation to 'feel free to use it' and the GitHub mention, which is not an explicit license statement
Page is a personal story; it gives no benchmark numbers for speed gains
The author notes the approach may need revisiting as the project grows
